info.title: simple-web-scraper
info.summary: Scrape pages in a real browser; get their main content as markdown.
info.description:
Loads web pages in a real headless Chrome and returns their main content as markdown.

**Zones.** `/api/1.0/scrap` loads pages — one (`POST /scrap`) or several
(`POST /scrap/batch`). `/api/1.0/profile` is the browser's persistent profile —
`DELETE /profile` resets it. `/health` is the resident's liveness.

**Authentication.** Every `/api/1.0/*` call takes `Authorization: Bearer <SCRAPER_API_KEY>`.
With an empty `SCRAPER_API_KEY` the check is off — local development only. `/health` is
always open. Requests a browser sends from another origin are refused (403).

**Verdicts, not HTTP errors.** A scrape that fails on the target's side — blocked, not
found, timed out — still returns HTTP 200; the verdict is in `outcome`. An HTTP error means
the request itself was rejected (400, 401, 403, 422) or the browser worker could not serve
it (500).

**Cold start.** The first call after idle starts the browser worker, about one to two
seconds on top of the scrape.

**No URL filtering.** The browser opens whatever URL it is given, internal addresses and
`file://` paths included. Keep the API on 127.0.0.1 and set a key.

Guide — modes, verdicts, limits, errors: `docs/api.md` in the repository.

get.description:
Answers without authentication and without touching the browser worker: the resident
is up, which does not promise that a scrape would succeed.

post.description:
Load the page in the browser and return its main content as markdown, with the
verdict in `outcome` (see `ScrapOutcome`). `use_idle` and `use_scroll` change how the
page is loaded.

200.description: The scrape result; the verdict is in `outcome`.

403.description: Sent by a browser from another origin (`Origin` differs from `Host`), code `origin_refused`. Programs send no `Origin` and are not affected.

401.description: Missing or wrong bearer token. Only when `SCRAPER_API_KEY` is set.

500.description: The browser worker failed or could not be reached, even after one respawn and retry. Plain text, not JSON.

post.description:
Load the pages in parallel with shared options and return one result per URL, in
request order.

A URL that fails inside the worker comes back as `internal` instead of failing the
batch. For the idle timers the whole batch is one request, and it shares one
resident→worker timeout.

200.description: One result per URL, in request order.

403.description: Sent by a browser from another origin (`Origin` differs from `Host`), code `origin_refused`. Programs send no `Origin` and are not affected.

401.description: Missing or wrong bearer token. Only when `SCRAPER_API_KEY` is set.

400.description: `urls` is empty once empty strings are dropped.

500.description: The browser worker failed or could not be reached, even after one respawn and retry. Plain text, not JSON.

delete.description:
Delete the persistent browser profile (`runtime/profile/`: cookies, cache, local
storage), closing the browser first; the next scrape starts with a fresh one. Works
whether or not the browser is running — the worker is started if needed.

It does not wait for scrapes in flight, it cuts them off: a single `/scrap` in progress
fails, batch items in progress come back as `internal`. Use it after switching
`SCRAPER_PROFILE`. Nothing restores a deleted profile.

403.description: Sent by a browser from another origin (`Origin` differs from `Host`), code `origin_refused`. Programs send no `Origin` and are not affected.

401.description: Missing or wrong bearer token. Only when `SCRAPER_API_KEY` is set.

500.description: The browser worker failed or could not be reached, even after one respawn and retry. Plain text, not JSON.

type.title: Type
type.description: Error class; `invalid_request_error` for every error the API raises itself.

code.title: Code
code.description: Machine-readable code, e.g. `invalid_api_key`; null when there is none.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description:
Error envelope of 400, 401 and 403 responses.

Request-body validation errors (422) use FastAPI's `{"detail": [...]}` format instead.

urls.title: Urls
urls.description: Pages to scrape; empty strings are dropped. They load in parallel: at most `SCRAPE_BATCH_CONCURRENCY` from this batch at once, within the worker's `PAGE_CONCURRENCY` page slots that all requests share. The whole call has one resident→worker timeout (`DAEMON_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, 180 s by default) — size batches to fit it.

use_idle.title: Use Idle
use_idle.description: Wait for network idle instead of `DOMContentLoaded`: for JS-rendered pages and SPAs that fill in after DOM ready. Slower; `timeout` still caps the wait.

use_scroll.title: Use Scroll
use_scroll.description: After the load, scroll to the bottom with a kinetic gesture: for lazy-loaded and infinite feeds. The scroll takes what is left of `timeout` after the load, at least 0.5 s.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: Budget in whole seconds, 1 to 60, for loading the page: the wait for `DOMContentLoaded` (network idle with `use_idle`) and the scroll with `use_scroll`. Whatever loaded by then is still read and extracted. A page that stops answering is abandoned at `timeout` + 15 s and reported as `timeout`.

ScrapBatchRequest.title: ScrapBatchRequest
ScrapBatchRequest.description: Scrape several pages in one call; the options apply to every URL.

results.title: Results
results.description: One result per URL, in request order (after dropping empty strings). A URL that failed inside the worker comes back as `internal`; the batch itself does not fail.

elapsed_ms.title: Elapsed Ms
elapsed_ms.description: Wall time of the whole batch in the worker, in milliseconds.

ScrapBatchResponse.title: ScrapBatchResponse
ScrapBatchResponse.description: Results of a batch, one per URL.

ScrapOutcome.description:
Verdict on the scrape — check it before using `content`. A failed scrape still comes back as HTTP 200, with the failure stated here.

- `ok` — usable main content, also when the load cap fired but enough content had already loaded.
- `redirected` — as `ok`, but the page ended on a different URL (`final_url`).
- `not_found` — the target answered 404.
- `access_denied` — the target answered 401, 403 or 429, or returned a short bot-wall or challenge page (Cloudflare, captcha).
- `upstream_error` — any other 4xx or 5xx from the target.
- `upstream_down` — no HTTP response: DNS or connection failure, or a resource the browser does not render as a page, such as a direct PDF.
- `empty` — a response, but under 200 characters of main content, typically a JS shell; retry with `use_idle`.
- `timeout` — the load cap fired before enough content loaded, or the page stopped answering and was abandoned.
- `internal` — this URL failed inside the worker; batch only, the other URLs are unaffected.

url.title: Url
url.description: Absolute URL of the page, passed to the browser as is.

use_idle.title: Use Idle
use_idle.description: Wait for network idle instead of `DOMContentLoaded`: for JS-rendered pages and SPAs that fill in after DOM ready. Slower; `timeout` still caps the wait.

use_scroll.title: Use Scroll
use_scroll.description: After the load, scroll to the bottom with a kinetic gesture: for lazy-loaded and infinite feeds. The scroll takes what is left of `timeout` after the load, at least 0.5 s.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: Budget in whole seconds, 1 to 60, for loading the page: the wait for `DOMContentLoaded` (network idle with `use_idle`) and the scroll with `use_scroll`. Whatever loaded by then is still read and extracted. A page that stops answering is abandoned at `timeout` + 15 s and reported as `timeout`.

url.title: Url
url.description: The requested URL, exactly as sent — match results by it.

final_url.title: Final Url
final_url.description: URL the page ended on after redirects. `about:blank` when the navigation never started (`timeout`); null when the page was abandoned or failed (`internal`).

target_status.title: Target Status
target_status.description: HTTP status of the page's main document; null when there was no response (connection failure, the load cap fired first, abandoned page).

title.title: Title
title.description: The document `<title>`; empty or null when the page could not be read.

headers.title: Headers
headers.description: Response headers of the main document, lower-case names; null when there was no response.

content.title: Content
content.description: Main content as markdown: trafilatura removes navigation, headers, footers and similar boilerplate; links and tables are kept, images dropped. Filled whatever the `outcome` — on `access_denied` it is the text of the wall. Null when nothing could be extracted.

body.title: Body
body.description: Rendered HTML of the page (the DOM after load), unprocessed — for debugging or your own extraction. Can be large.

redirects.title: Redirects
redirects.description: Reserved for intermediate redirect URLs; always empty for now.

elapsed_ms.title: Elapsed Ms
elapsed_ms.description: Time spent on this URL in the worker, in milliseconds, including the wait for a free page slot.

ScrapResponse.title: ScrapResponse
ScrapResponse.description:
Result of one scrape.

Read `outcome` first: `content` is filled whatever the verdict, so a bot wall or an
error page comes with text too.
